numbers.name: clear_room_height_min_m
numbers.source: Musterbauordnung (MBO) §47(1): Aufenthaltsräume need a clear height of at least 2.40 m

numbers.name: storey_height_typical_m
numbers.source: Derived: MBO §47(1) 2.40 m clear height plus approx. 0.35 m floor/slab build-up, on the DIN 4172 12.5 cm module (https://www.baunetzwissen.de/glossar/m/massordnung-48043)

numbers.name: roof_pitch_typical_deg
numbers.source: https://www.hausjournal.net/dachneigung-satteldach (German gable roofs typically 35-45 deg; older steep roofs to 60+ deg); consistent with assets_src/refs/wgerman_town_block_1989/ refs

numbers.name: building_footprint_short_side_median_m
numbers.source: Measured from OpenStreetMap building footprints (ODbL) within 300 m of Am Alten Rathaus, Ober-Erlenbach, Overpass query 2026-10-08: 494 buildings >50 m2, IQR 7.7-11.4 m

numbers.name: plot_width_typical_m
numbers.source: Derived estimate: footprint long side 12.9 m (OSM, above) plus one 3 m minimum boundary distance (Hessische Bauordnung §6 minimum Abstandsfläche 3 m); old-core Hofreite plots built to one boundary. Needs a cadastral check.

signature_features: Steep red clay-tile gable roofs (35-60 deg) with dormers, plus slate-hung gables and mansard roofs on 19th-century houses
Half-timbered (Fachwerk) frontages with exposed red/brown timber framing over a sandstone or plinth ground floor
Plastered postwar 2-3 storey houses in pale render with shutters, small windows in regular bays
Hofreite courtyard farmsteads with large arched sandstone gateways (Hoftor) set between houses on the street line
1960s-80s infill: flat-fronted commercial buildings with balconies, shop windows and a Gasthaus sign on the corner
